candidate_relations.label: mild Gastritis
candidate_relations.reason: The endoscopy revealed mild gastritis, but this finding does not explain the episodic nature of the pain, the preceding visual and auditory hallucinations, or the epileptiform EEG activity. Mild gastritis is at most an incidental or contributing finding, not the final diagnostic entity requested. The benchmark diagnosis integrates the neurological workup (EEG epileptiform activity), the post-COVID temporal relationship, and the episodic abdominal pain with aura-like symptoms.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mild gastritis is an incidental endoscopic finding in this case, not the primary diagnosis; the reference diagnosis is abdominal epilepsy as a sequela of COVID-19, supported by epileptiform EEG activity in the right temporo-occipital region and the clinical context of post-COVID neurological sequelae.

case_quality_flags: EEG epileptiform activity in right temporo-occipital region is the key discriminating finding supporting abdominal epilepsy over a gastrointestinal etiology
Post-COVID-19 neurological sequela context is essential to the reference diagnosis and absent from the candidate
Mild gastritis is an incidental endoscopic finding inconsistent with the episodic aura-preceded pain pattern
